findings.claim: The new unreadable-transcript path attributes a parse failure only when path.parent.name equals slug = "-" + "-".join(repo.strip("/").split("/")), which substitutes only "/". The lane's documented Claude encoding replaces every "/" and "." (ops/process/cross-review.md:162; ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/launch_support.py:698-699). Source-stamped on this dispatch snapshot path: worth slug keeps ".local" as -home-scientdb-.local-state-... while claude_slug emits -home-scientdb--local-state-..., equal=False. Dot-free paths match. Dispatch snapshots under .local therefore never match, so include_unreadable skips the file instead of emitting turns/avg_context/refusals="unrecorded". Slice point 2 and docs/wire.md absence discipline fail: "could not look" reads as "found nothing". Readable rows still filter by cwd (worth.py:115) and are unaffected. When the slash-only slug does match, the same block has no cwd or timestamp, so colliding paths share the id and the row is treated as a known session in every window; usage.py:94 already says cwd is the truth for a lossy slug. cmd_waste then sorts no-total rows last (worth.py:697) and truncates to --top (default 5), so even a matched unreadable row can vanish from the default listing. Not P1 under D-LAUNCHER-1 / I-010 (no job escape, no lane-integrity break); P2 because it defeats the new waste-row guarantee on ordinary dotted lane paths. Source: python3 comparison of the two slug formulas on this snapshot path, plus sed of worth.py:99-108 and launch_support.py:698-699. Unexecuted behavioral hypothesis: plant '{broken\n' under the claude_slug directory and call claude_sessions(..., include_unreadable=True); expected sessions={}, not unrecorded.

findings.claim: The new session-budget fields are taken from contexts, appended for every in-window assistant usage row (worth.py:131-135) before last-wins in_window[mid] (136-139). turns=len(contexts) and avg_context=sum/len (167-168) therefore count Claude re-emissions that the same function collapses for token totals. usage.py:80-81 records the live store as 2086 usage lines over 1052 ids, so inflated turns are the normal shape, not an edge. The append also adds usage.get(..., 0) values before replacement; dict.get does not replace an explicit null, and the loop catches only ValueError (140), not TypeError. A non-int or null on an earlier emission, even if a later same-id row is valid, aborts the whole meter instead of recording the transcript unrecorded. Slice/worth.md require last-wins for Claude ids and unreadable/malformed as unrecorded, never a crash. The parenthetical "assistant usage rows" is ambiguous against that last-wins rule; the function already chose last-wins for the related figures. Not P1: a telemetry TypeError does not escape a job or break dispatch. P2 because both the wrong turn count and the abort fire on ordinary vendor transcripts. Source: python3 inspection of claude_sessions (contexts_append_before_mid True; except TypeError absent; {"input_tokens": None}.get(..., 0) is None; None+0 and "bad"+0 are TypeError). Unexecuted behavioral hypothesis: two in-window rows with one message id yield messages=1 and turns=2; then input_tokens="bad" followed by 300 raises TypeError rather than unrecorded.

findings.claim: New helper _tool_result_denied counts a tool_result whose stringified content contains "hook returned a deny decision" and does not inspect is_error or any deny/status field. The same telemetry package classifies tool_result errors via is_error (breaker.py:163). The marker string is literal in this helper, so a successful Read of worth.py itself matches. Slice says "tool-result deny markers"; the Grok tests plant is_error true on both the deny and the command-error and never plant a successful payload containing the marker. False refusals therefore appear on ordinary sessions that read this repo. Not P1 under D-LAUNCHER-1. P2 because the new waste field is a live token-thrift signal and the false positive is this tree's own source. Source: sed of worth.py:82-91 (no is_error) and breaker.py:163. Unexecuted behavioral hypothesis: message content [{"type":"tool_result","is_error":False,"content": <worth.py text>}] makes _tool_result_denied return True.
